A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a novel deep learning algorithm to predict esophageal wall thickness and the esophagus spatial presentation over time, using a multimodal imaging dataset acquired during the radiotherapy course.
we developed a machine learning algorithm that predicts spatial esophageal wall changes over time using MRI/CBCT scans acquired earlier in a radiotherapy treatment course.
our approach is able to predict esophageal changes over a 6 week radio therapy course with high accuracy, and can be applied to both MRI and CBCT data.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a combination of convolutional and recurrent neural networks can be used to predict the spatial presentation of a structure of interest, in this case the esophagus, in a time series of medical images.

a combination of convolutional and recurrent neural networks, trained on MRI scans, can be used to predict the spatial presentation of the irradiated esophagus in CBCT scans acquired later in the treatment course.

a convolutional recurrent network can be trained using a limited set of MRI scans to accurately predict future esophageal changes, and can be used to reconstruct the spatial esophageal response patterns in the weeks to follow.
